title: edikt plan criteria sidecar
description: Spec-only criteria sidecar (PLAN-<slug>-criteria.yaml) consumed by `edikt verify`. Mirrors tools/edikt/internal/verify/schema.go, which strict-decodes (KnownFields) — any field not listed here makes verify exit 2. Evaluation state (status, fail_count, fail_reason, …) does NOT belong in this file; it lives in .edikt/state/plan-eval/PLAN-<slug>-eval.json (see plan-eval-state.v1.schema.json). Two constraints live only in the Go validator, which remains authoritative: phase ids must be unique across the file, and criterion ids must be unique within a phase. Ids and created accept unquoted YAML scalars (numbers, dates) because Go's yaml.v3 coerces scalars into string fields; quoting them is still the recommended style.

schema_version.description: Discrete integer version (same convention as gov-sidecar.v1): the shape is a v1-or-v2 contract, not semver-evolved.

created.description: ISO-8601 date. Untyped on purpose: unquoted YAML dates parse as date objects, and the Go decoder accepts them into its string field.

id.description: Phase identifier, unique across the file. Unquoted numeric ids are accepted (yaml.v3 coerces them to string); quoting (id: "1") is the recommended style.

classification.description: testable = every criterion carries an executable verify command; operational = observable but not machine-checkable; informational = context only; owner = completion is a human decision (a ruling, a sign-off, a go/no-go) and the criteria are never executed. owner is deliberately distinct from informational: informational means there is nothing to check, owner means a person must act and may not have, and a report scanned for outstanding human work must be able to tell them apart.

phase_metadata.description: Freeform, runner-ignored. Nothing in `edikt verify` reads this. It exists because this schema is validated with additionalProperties:false and the loader decodes with KnownFields(true), so before it existed a plan carrying any concept the schema had not anticipated could not be loaded at all — leaving the author to delete their own text or mislabel the phase. Put the unanticipated thing here instead; it survives in the file where its author put it.

id.description: Criterion identifier, unique within the phase, e.g. AC-2.1. Unquoted numeric ids (id: 1.1) are accepted; quoting is the recommended style.

verify.description: Shell command exiting 0 when the criterion holds. Required when the phase is testable; omit the key entirely (never verify: null) otherwise.

requirements.description: OPTIONAL list of the spec ids this criterion claims to satisfy — requirement ids (SR-*) or protection ids (SSP-*) drawn from the spec sidecar of the spec the plan implements. OPTIONAL here and REQUIRED by the coverage gate, never the reverse: this file is consumed under strict decoding, so a required field would stop every existing criteria file in every downstream project from loading on upgrade, turning a coverage improvement into a breaking change. An empty list is the explicit "this criterion satisfies no requirement" declaration, which is not the same as omitting the key. A declaration records that a requirement is CLAIMED, NOT that the criterion asserts the property: the coverage gate closes the absence case only, and whether a claim holds is a reading rather than a check. Ids absent from the plan's spec are rejected by the Go loader, which names them.

verify_kind.description: Cheat-rate scoring metadata (structural | behavioral). The Go decoder does not constrain the value.

timeout_s.description: Optional per-criterion timeout in seconds, overriding the runner's 30 s default for a criterion that legitimately runs longer (a release gate, an install-and-upgrade path). Absent means the default. Added 2026-09-02 (PLAN-v090-release Phase 0): without it the runner recorded such criteria as timeout and a release plan could never flip its own gate.

dependencies.description: Optional DAG edges between phases, keyed by phase id.
